explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/682: for almost all n is there m ∈ (p_n, p_{n+1}) with least prime factor p(m) ≥ p_{n+1} − p_n? Solved affirmatively by Gafni–Tao. The statement says the set of such n has natural density 1, with p the 0-indexed nth prime and minFac the least prime factor (m ≥ 4 in these intervals, so minFac is genuine). The index shift does not affect density. Faithful.
